entries.title: Ports declared in barrels are not implemented by the concrete services

evidence.detail: users.service.ts / holders.service.ts / tenants.service.ts declare no implements clause.

notes: 2026-10-04 part 2: intent-based ports with implements; lockout policy owned by users; auth uses TokenBlacklistPort; facade has a consumer
entries.detail: UsersPort/HoldersPort/TenantsPort live inside index.ts and the services (UsersService, HoldersService, TenantsService) never `implements` them. Compatibility is structural only, so a service change can silently break the contract at the composition root instead of failing to compile.

entries.title: Validation logic and messages duplicated across five services

evidence.detail: Same if(!email)/EMAIL_REGEX/PASSWORD_REGEX blocks repeated in auth.service.ts, users.service.ts, holders.service.ts.

entries.detail: Although EMAIL_REGEX/PASSWORD_REGEX/OBJECTID_REGEX now live in common/constants/regex, the surrounding guard-and-error logic is copied in AuthService (login/signup/reset), UsersService, HoldersService, CodesService and RefreshTokenService. Changing a rule or message still forces edits in five-plus files; no email/password value object owns the policy.

entries.title: Reset-password code stores a User id in holderId with ref 'Holder'

evidence.detail: auth.service.ts:178-180 createForgotPasswordCode(user._id); codes.service.ts:62 create(userId, RESET_PASSWORD).

entries.detail: CodesService.create always writes to field holderId with ref 'Holder', but forgot-password passes a User id. The field name and mongoose ref no longer describe what is stored for RESET_PASSWORD codes, an implicit assumption shared between auth and codes.

entries.title: Holder expiry and code expiry share CODE_EXPIRATION_MS

evidence.detail: codes.service.ts:19 also reads CODE_EXPIRATION_MS.

entries.detail: HoldersSchema derives its TTL from CODE_EXPIRATION_MS, the same env var that CodesService uses for one-time codes. Two unrelated concepts share one undeclared constant; changing code lifetime silently changes holder lifetime.

entries.title: updateOneById(Partial<User>) lets auth write internal user fields

evidence.detail: updateOneById(id: string, updateData: Partial<User>) exposed on UsersPort.

notes: 2026-10-04 part 2: intent-based ports with implements; lockout policy owned by users; auth uses TokenBlacklistPort; facade has a consumer
entries.detail: AuthService resets loginAttempts/lockoutUntil through UsersPort.updateOneById(id, Partial<User>), so auth must know the user representation and can mutate any field (including password) without going through users' invariants (e.g. hashing is implicit). This is Tell-Don't-Ask broken across the boundary.

entries.title: common RequiredBodyMiddleware hardcodes the /auth/logout route

evidence.detail: required-body.middleware.ts:3 hardcodes an auth endpoint path.

entries.detail: A generic common middleware embeds knowledge of an auth route via EXCLUDED_PATHS = ['/auth/logout']. This is the same class of shared-boundary assumption the TokenBlacklistPort refactor removed: common should be route-agnostic and receive the exclusion policy from the caller.

entries.title: users port depends on holders' entity type

evidence.detail: users/index.ts imports { Holder } from '../holders'.

notes: 2026-10-04 part 2: intent-based ports with implements; lockout policy owned by users; auth uses TokenBlacklistPort; facade has a consumer
entries.detail: UsersPort.createFromHolder(holder: Holder) makes the users module import the holders entity type, coupling two modules through a concrete representation instead of an explicit primitive (for example a VerifiedEmail value with email and password).

entries.title: Mailer port mixes a general mechanism with business policy

evidence.detail: nodemailer.adapter.ts:7 imports { MailTemplate } from '../../../mail/mail.enum'.

entries.detail: MailerInterface couples generic delivery (sendEmail/sendMailWithTemplate) with specific policy (sendWelcomeEmail/sendSignupVerificationEmail/sendResetPasswordEmail). The nodemailer adapter also imports MailTemplate from the mail/ domain folder, so infrastructure depends on a business enum. General mechanism and specific policy should be split.

entries.title: CodesService reads CODE_EXPIRATION_MS and CODE_LENGTH from env instead of being injected

evidence.detail: codes.service.ts:19-20 getNumberEnvVariable('CODE_EXPIRATION_MS'/'CODE_LENGTH'); jwt.service.ts receives expiresIn injected.

entries.detail: Unlike JwtService (which receives expiry via constructor), CodesService reads two env vars directly in its constructor. Config-injection policy is inconsistent across libs/modules and the code lifetime is a hidden global rather than a declared constructor contract.

entries.title: Lockout policy parameters pushed onto UsersPort

evidence.detail: auth.service.ts:91-95 forwards this.maxLoginAttempts and this.lockoutDurationMs.

notes: 2026-10-04 part 2: intent-based ports with implements; lockout policy owned by users; auth uses TokenBlacklistPort; facade has a consumer
entries.detail: incrementLoginAttempts(id, maxAttempts, lockoutDurationMs) requires the caller (AuthService) to pass the lockout policy on every failed login. The policy is decided once at the composition root, then threaded through two layers; the common case should be a domain default owned by users.

entries.title: AuthModule is a composition magnet with 15 constructor parameters

evidence.detail: application.composition.ts:111-129 passes 15 positional arguments.

entries.detail: AuthModule receives usersService, cryptoService, jwtService, logger, mailService, codeService, authenticationMiddleware, refreshTokenService, blacklistService, holdersService, authTenantService plus maxLoginAttempts, lockoutDurationMs, rateLimitConfig and publicAppUrl, then constructs SessionService/AuthService/AuthController itself. Wiring, policy and construction are mixed; the caller must know every collaborator to build auth.

entries.title: auth/index.ts facade is unused and exports concrete internals

evidence.detail: No import of '../auth' exists in src/ or test/.

notes: 2026-10-04 part 2: intent-based ports with implements; lockout policy owned by users; auth uses TokenBlacklistPort; facade has a consumer
entries.detail: The barrel exports AuthModule and the concrete AuthService, yet no file imports from '../auth'. Cross-module consumers bypass the facade entirely (auth.module imports users/holders indexes directly), so the boundary is undefined and the concrete class is the de-facto contract.

entries.title: RefreshTokenService.findAllActiveByUserId has no production consumer

evidence.detail: rg shows only test/integration/src/auth/tokens/refresh-tokens.service.test.ts references.

entries.detail: The method is used only by integration tests; no production path lists active tokens. Either wire it or drop it to keep the surface honest.

entries.title: common owns codes/auth domain exception taxonomy

evidence.detail: common/exceptions/{codes,auth}.exceptions.ts define auth/business failures.

entries.detail: AlreadyGeneratedCodeError/InvalidCodeError live in common/exceptions/codes.exceptions.ts and UnauthorizedError/InvalidCredentialsError/AccountLockedError in auth.exceptions.ts. A shared BaseError kernel is legitimate, but codes/auth domain failures belong to their modules; common should only hold genuinely cross-cutting infra errors (as InfraError does).

entries.title: AuthService depends on concrete BlacklistService instead of the port

evidence.detail: constructor(... blacklistService: BlacklistService ...) and auth.module.ts:35 passes BlacklistService.

notes: 2026-10-04 part 2: intent-based ports with implements; lockout policy owned by users; auth uses TokenBlacklistPort; facade has a consumer
entries.detail: The port TokenBlacklistPort exists and BlacklistService implements it, yet AuthService and AuthModule type the dependency as the concrete class, so the boundary is weaker than it needs to be.

entries.title: JwtService exposed a domain-named operation (issueSession)

evidence.detail: Before: issueSession(userId, role): TokenPair; after: signTokenPair(userId, role): TokenPair. Sole production caller is SessionService.

notes: 2026-10-04 renamed issueSession -> signTokenPair; SessionService owns session semantics
entries.detail: The technical signing lib named a method issueSession, borrowing the session concept that belongs to SessionService. Naming mixed interface nature (technical lib vs domain concept). Renamed to signTokenPair so libs/jwt stays technical and session semantics live only in SessionService.

entries.title: AuthTenantService duplicates ObjectId validation and compares secrets directly

evidence.detail: tenants.service.ts:14 re-validates with OBJECTID_REGEX; auth-tenant reads tenant.active and tenant.secret.

entries.detail: AuthTenantService validates tenantId with Types.ObjectId.isValid and then calls TenantsPort.findById, which validates the same id again. It also reads tenant.active/tenant.secret directly, so tenant representation leaks into auth. The check belongs in tenants (verifyCredentials) or a dedicated operation.

entries.title: AuthService constructor mixes orchestration, lockout policy and deployment URL

evidence.detail: publicAppUrl default 'https://ourservice.com' used in signup/forgotPassword link building (lines 152,186).

entries.detail: AuthService takes ten collaborators including maxLoginAttempts/lockoutDurationMs (policy owned elsewhere) and publicAppUrl with a hardcoded default. The URL builds mail links inside the domain service, leaking a deployment concern into orchestration.

entries.title: AuthModule exposes service/controller/tenantsController that nobody reads

evidence.detail: Only authModule.initialize(app) is called in application.composition.ts:140.

entries.detail: The public fields are declared but the composition root only calls initialize(app). They are pass-through exports with no consumer; the real entry point is initialize.

entries.title: CodesService signup/forgot-password creators are 1:1 wrappers

evidence.detail: codes.service.ts:58-64 delegate directly to create().

entries.detail: createSignupCode and createForgotPasswordCode add no behavior over create(holderId, type); they only rename. They are intent-revealing but add a hop without hiding complexity.

entries.title: TenantsService.findById is a pass-through wrapper

evidence.detail: tenants.service.ts:18 returns this.tenantsModel.findById(id).lean().exec().

entries.detail: The entire module is one method whose body is a single findById().lean().exec(). Signature is equivalent to the body; it earns its boundary only when a second tenant operation appears.

entries.title: codes index built on nonexistent userId path (legacy finding)

evidence.detail: codes.schema.ts:20 -> CodesSchema.index({ holderId: 1, type: 1, used: 1 }).

entries.detail: The lookup index was previously declared on `userId` while the document field is `holderId`, leaving the (holderId,type,used) query unindexed. Now corrected to `holderId`.

entries.title: JwtService.verifyToken leaked jsonwebtoken union

evidence.detail: verifyToken(token: string): TokenClaims; consumers read userId/role/jti without casting.

entries.detail: verifyToken used to return JwtPayload | string, forcing casts at every caller. It now returns the domain TokenClaims type.

entries.title: common imported auth blacklist concrete class (layering inversion)

evidence.detail: authentication.middleware.ts imports ../../libs/jwt and ../ports/token-blacklist.port.

entries.detail: Authentication middleware previously imported auth/tokens/blacklist.service. It now depends on the TokenBlacklistPort owned by common; BlacklistService implements it.

entries.title: findById advertised |null but threw EntityNotFoundError

evidence.detail: findById returns this.usersModel.findById(id); auth.service.ts checks if (!user).

entries.detail: UsersService/HoldersService findById declared Promise<X | null> yet threw on miss, so callers kept dead null checks. They now return null and callers genuinely branch on it.

entries.title: JwtService exposes unused generate* wrappers and duplicate jti logic

evidence.detail: rg shows generateAccessToken/generateRefreshToken/generateTokens used only in tests; signUserToken duplicates generateToken's validation.

notes: 2026-10-04 public surface reduced to issueSession + generateTenantToken + verifyToken
entries.detail: The public surface has generateToken, generateAccessToken, generateRefreshToken, generateTenantToken, generateTokens, issueSession and signUserToken. Production uses only issueSession and generateTenantToken; generateAccessToken/generateRefreshToken/generateTokens are test-only and their jti logic duplicates issueSession/signUserToken. The interface is nearly as broad as the implementation.

entries.title: libs/config-service is an unwired dead abstraction

evidence.detail: rg for config-service/ConfigService outside src/libs/config-service/** returns nothing.

notes: 2026-10-04 deleted unwired libs/config-service and its tests/fixtures
entries.detail: config-service.interface.ts, its Mongo adapter and schema have zero production wiring and no consumers outside their own folder. It is pure maintenance cost until a real dynamic-config need exists.

entries.title: Session issuance was split by execution order across AuthService

evidence.detail: AuthService now calls sessionService.create/rotate; JwtService.issueSession returns { accessToken, refreshToken, refreshTokenId, refreshExpiresAt }.

entries.detail: The generate -> verify -> revoke -> persist sequence was duplicated across login and refresh within AuthService. Extracted into SessionService.create/rotate with JwtService.issueSession returning TokenPair metadata.

entries.title: tenants interface file is misspelled tentants.interface.ts

evidence.detail: tenants/index.ts and tenants.service.ts import './tentants.interface'.

entries.detail: The filename `tentants.interface.ts` is imported by tenants/index.ts and tenants.service.ts. Renaming removes a permanent naming wart at low risk.

entries.title: NodeMailerAdapter mutates the caller's template context

evidence.detail: context.appName = this.appName; context.year = this.year in three methods.

notes: 2026-10-04 NodeMailerAdapter clones context instead of mutating it
entries.detail: sendWelcomeEmail/sendSignupVerificationEmail/sendResetPasswordEmail write appName and year onto the caller-supplied context object, so the caller's data is silently mutated. The adapter should copy the context before enriching it.

entries.title: WinstonLogger.logger exposes the concrete winston.Logger

evidence.detail: public logger: Logger (winston) on the adapter.

notes: 2026-10-04 WinstonLogger.logger and createLogger are now private
entries.detail: The adapter declares a public `logger: winston.Logger` field, exposing the concrete logging library to anyone holding the logger. The LoggerInterface port is the intended surface; the field should be private.
